summary: Iteration 39 (DM Unread Count badge) backend-only review. 16/16 pytest test cases pass against the new GET /api/community/dm/unread-count endpoint and the regression set. Covered: (1) 401 without bearer & with invalid token, (2) {total:0, threads:[]} for fresh non-admin user, (3) end-to-end 1:1 flow (admin → 3 msgs → non-admin sees total=3 with matching thread_id/unread=3 → opening thread mark-reads → count drops to 0), (4) sender's own unread stays 0 (admin's count remains 0 after sending), (5) group DM with admin+non-admin+third → admin sends 2 msgs → both non-admin AND third see unread=2 for thread → non-admin opens thread → non-admin drops to 0 but third remains at unread=2, (6) regression on /community/dm/threads list+create, /community/dm/threads/{tid}/messages POST+GET, /subscriptions/status admin/free, /auth/me admin/free, /library/books, /library/films, humanae-vitae chapter 0 (non-admin 200), confessions-augustine chapter 0 (non-admin 402). The endpoint correctly excludes sender_id == user.user_id and uses thread.reads[user_id] as the last_read_at watermark.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2243-2263 dm_unread_count implementation is clean and correct: filters threads by member_ids, applies $gt last_read_at watermark, excludes sender_id == user.user_id. Cost is O(threads) count_documents calls (limit 500) — fine for current scale but if user can have hundreds of threads, consider a single aggregation pipeline ($lookup + $project) to collapse to one round-trip.

Subtle race: if admin sends a message at the exact same epoch ms that the receiver's read-mark was written, the $gt comparison will tie-exclude that message (unread will be 0). In practice impossible because reads are written by the receiver opening the thread (their msg send is separate) but worth noting if a future code path bulk-writes both.
server.py is now 3070 lines — over the 700-line guideline. The DM/community routes (~1000 lines) are the obvious candidate to extract into a router module before further growth.
